Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Planning Commission on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules and proceedings described in Section 2.16.060 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address the Planning Commission, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to
the Secretary. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to
a vote. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
future Planning Commission meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Planning Commission:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Planning Commission as a whole and not directed to individual Planning Commission members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when
services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or
service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Planning Commission regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

   MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL ADJOURNED MEETING
  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  JANUARY 8, 2025

The meeting was called to order by Chair Lopez at 6:00 p.m., in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were
Commissioner Vernola-Salas, Vice Chair Apodaca, and Chair Lopez. Commissioner
Barragan was absent. Also present were Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of Community
Development; Gloria V. Ramirez, Deputy City Attorney; Kristy Wong, Associate Planner;
and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

REORGANIZATION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION

By unanimous voice vote, Linda Lopez was re-appointed as Chair, and Kim Apodaca was
re-appointed as Vice-Chair of the Planning Commission for the upcoming year.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Planning Commission
Meeting of November 25, 2024.

PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN NO. 2023-06
Ben Martin, Rexford Industrial Realty LP (“Applicant”); a request to demolish two existing
multi-tenant industrial warehouse buildings totaling 89,870 square feet to construct a
new 138,972± square foot industrial warehouse building with off-street parking,
landscaping improvements, and associated infrastructure on a 7.03-acre lot located at
14830 Carmenita Road (Assessor’s Parcel Number (APN) 8069-002-085), in the Heavy
Manufacturing (M2) zone. The proposed building would include 132,227 square feet of
warehouse space, 3,715 square feet of ground-floor office space, and 3,030 square feet
of mezzanine office space.
Environmental: Review and adoption of Mitigated Negative Declaration with the
Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Plan.

After opening the continued public hearing, Chair Lopez announced that the applicant
has submitted a request for continuation of Precise Development Plan No. 2023-06 to
the meeting of February 12, 2025.

As there were no objections, it was moved by Vice Chair Apodaca and seconded by
Commissioner Vernola-Salas to continue the public hearing of Precise Development
Plan No. 2023-06 to the meeting of February 12, 2025, as requested by the applicant.

ON ROLL CALL VOTE:
AYES:  Commissioner Vernola-Salas, Vice Chair Apodaca and Chair Lopez
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Commissioner Barragan
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Minutes of the Special Adjourned Meeting  January 8, 2025

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development, congratulated Linda Lopez
and Kim Apodaca on being re-appointed as Chair and Vice-Chair, respectively, for the
upcoming year. Further, he shared that he is looking forward to working with the Planning
Commission and ramping up activities.

ADJOURNMENT

There being no further business, the meeting adjourned at 6:05 p.m.

  LINDA LOPEZ, CHAIR

TO:  Planning Commission

FROM:  Alex Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development

BY:  Nancy Lee, Development Services Manager

SUBJECT: Senate Bill 9 Study Session

Introduction/background:

Senate Bill 9

Introduced by Senator Toni Atkins on December 7, 2020 and approved by Governor Gavin
Newsom on September 16, 2021, Senate Bill (SB) 9 became effective on January 1, 2022
and is one of many methods that the State is using to address the statewide housing
shortage. SB 9 requires local agencies to ministerially approve the following:

  •  SB 9 Units – For properties located in the single-family zones and meet applicable
  requirements, State Law requires that cities ministerially approve a maximum of two
  primary units per parcel.
  •  Urban Lot Split – For properties located in the single-family zones, the ministerial
  approval of the subdivision of one parcel into two parcels.

SB 9 units may be considered with or without an Urban Lot Split. If SB 9 units are proposed
in conjunction with an Urban Lot Split, SB 9 would facilitate the creation of up to four housing
units on property typically used for one single-family dwelling. In addition, SB 9 is meant to
be complementary to Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) laws, therefore, as the State Law is
written, SB 9 primary units and ADUs may be constructed together on the same parcel.

SB 9 Development Standards

Local agencies may impose objective zoning, subdivision, and design review standards as
long as such standards do not physically preclude the ability of a property owner to develop
 Planning Commission  Page 2
Senate Bill 9 Study Session  February 12, 2025

two primary units of at least 800 square feet in size. Examples of standards include (but are
not limited to):

SB 9 Units
  • Setbacks – Four feet for side and rear.
  • No setback required for an existing structure or proposed structure in the same
  location and the same dimensions as the existing structure.
  • Off-Street Parking – Maximum of one off-street parking space for each primary unit
  unless units are within one half-mile walking distance of a high-quality transit corridor
  or major transit stop or if there is a car share vehicle located within one block of the
  parcel.

  Urban Lot Splits
  • Creation of a maximum of two parcels in equal lot area, provided that one parcel shall
  not be smaller than 40 percent of the lot area of the original parcel proposed for
  subdivision.
  • Newly created parcels shall not be smaller than 1,200 square feet in size.
  •  Urban lot split conforms to the Subdivision Map Act.
  • City shall not require dedications of rights-of-way or the construction of off-site
  improvements.

SB 9 Restrictions
SB 9 restrictions are listed as follows:

  •  Correction of non-conforming zoning conditions.
  •  Demolition or alteration of existing rent-restricted housing units is prohibited or
  housing that has been occupied by a tenant in the last three years.
  •  Properties that have been occupied by a tenant the past three years are ineligible.
  •  Demolition of 25 percent of exterior walls would be prohibited if the site has been
  occupied by a tenant the past three years.
  •  Short term rentals of less than 30 days would be prohibited.
  •  Properties that were approved for an Urban Lot Split require an owner occupancy for
  a minimum of three years, unless the applicant is a community land trust or qualified
  nonprofit corporation.
  •  Properties where the property owner or any person acting in concert with the owner
  that has previously subdivided an adjacent parcel using the Urban Lot Split are not
  eligible.
  •  Properties located within a historic district are not eligible.

SB 9 allows local Building Officials to deny a duplex project by making a written finding, based
on a preponderance of evidence, that the project would have a specific adverse impact on
public health and safety or the physical environment, and that there is no feasible method to
 Planning Commission  Page 3
Senate Bill 9 Study Session  February 12, 2025

mitigate or avoid such an impact. A “specific adverse impact” must be significant,
quantifiable, direct and unavoidable, based on an objective written public health or safety
standard that existed at the time the project application was deemed complete. Inconsistency
with a city’s General Plan or zoning ordinance does not constitute a specific adverse impact.

Since SB 9 has been in effect, the Planning Division has been applying the current State Law
requirements for SB 9 applications. To date, the Planning Division has processed three SB
9 applications.

Discussion:

Staff is undergoing research to prepare an SB 9 ordinance which would bring the Norwalk
Zoning Code into alignment with standards as required by State Law, while establishing
objective zoning, subdivision, and design review standards that align with the City’s goals and
needs while maintaining as much local control as possible. Should the city fail to adopt an
ordinance in accordance with State SB 9 Law, the city may be limited to only applying State
Law standards without local refinements to SB 9 projects.

Per State Law, objective means standards that involve no personal or subjective judgment by
a public official and are uniformly verifiable by reference to an external and uniform benchmark
or criterion available and knowable by both the development applicant or proponent and the
public official prior to submittal.

Standards that may be considered as part of a local SB 9 ordinance include (but are not limited
to):

  •  Restricting ADU and JADU’s to be constructed in conjunction with SB 9
  developments.
  •  Building separation requirements.
  •  Limit the size of SB 9 units to an 800 square foot maximum.
  •  Enclosed parking stalls.
  •  Affordability restrictions of the SB 9 units.
  •  Single-story height limitation.
  •  Requirement of mature trees and live landscaping.
  •  Open space requirements.
  •  Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) construction standards
  for new SB 9 units.
  •  Requiring grey water systems, all electric “Energy Star” appliances, and cool roof
  technology.
  •  Restrictions of SB 9 developments on properties in the special districts, including
  areas where a high fire hazard or seismic risk exists.
 Planning Commission  Page 4
Senate Bill 9 Study Session  February 12, 2025

  •  Objective building design standards as they relate to exterior finish materials and
  design.
  •  Compliance with all LA County Fire Department requirements, including, but not
  limited to fire apparatus access roads and any additional access roads as may be
  required by the fire code official, fire sprinklers, fire alarms, including fire alarm
  monitoring, premises identification, and Fire Protection Water supplies including
  but not limited to Fire Hydrant Systems.

  Recommendation:

  Receive staff’s Senate Bill (SB) 9 presentation, provide feedback on potential SB 9
  standards and direct staff to return with a SB 9 ordinance and other Zoning Code Text
  amendments.
